Subject: SOC 2 re-attestation for renewal — initial ask

Hi Mina,

We're kicking off Orbis's annual vendor recert and want to understand scope for Redwood's SOC 2 re-attest for our upcoming renewal (Dec 1 renewal date). Two immediate asks: 1) confirmation of the log retention windows by region (we have EU residency requirements), and 2) a realistic timeline for evidence handoff (exported logs, traces, config artifacts).

I've attached a short questionnaire (Orbis_SOC2_Questions.xlsx) with our initial evidence checklist. On retention specifically: our auditors require a 90-day searchable window for privacy-sensitive EU customers and 365 days for US-resident accounts. Can Redwood support a split/segmented retention policy? If not, what's the alternative (escrow, snapshots, or other)?

Also note we're evaluating an increase to dedicated capacity (+25% seat uplift) tied to the renewal; procurement would like any compliance scope/changes to be reflected in the amendment.

Appreciate a proposal by Oct 15 so we can present to our security committee the week of Oct 18.

Thanks,
Sophie
Head of Vendor Risk — Orbis Financial

Attachment: Orbis_SOC2_Questions.xlsx

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Carter <s.carter@orbisfinancial.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation for renewal — initial ask

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear checklist and timeline. We're on it. High level: Redwood can support region-aware retention, but we need to align on implementation approach and terms. Options we can offer quickly:

- Native regional slicing: keep hot searchable logs in-region (EU) for 90 days and full 365-day retention in US; EU-exported logs would be redacted for PII if required. This requires an audit of current customer routing and will incur an operational delta charge (see Ben's note below).
- Snapshot escrow: nightly encrypted snapshots of the full index delivered to a secure escrow bucket in-region for auditor retrieval (adds a staging/transfer SLA).
- Hybrid: 90-day hot in-region + 365-day cold encrypted archive accessible via request (48–72h retrieval).

Operational ask from our side: 1) confirm which option you prefer, 2) confirm whether KMS/HSM proof is needed (we have KMS logs we can share), and 3) confirm the final retention durations (if different from 90/365).

I'll coordinate the evidence packaging cadence with Kimberly. Ben will propose the amendment language for the renewal and seat increase. If Oct 15 is the decision target, can we plan for a 1–2 day operational readiness check and a formal amendment draft by Oct 20?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Security Manager — Redwood Inference

CC: Kimberly — can you draft the evidence delivery plan? Laura — heads-up in case Legal needs to review retention carveouts.

Sophie — thanks for the spreadsheet, I reviewed the checklist and sketched an evidence handoff plan attached (redwood-log-retention-matrix.csv). Key operational notes:

- We can enable region-scoped hot retention per customer routing at the account level. For Orbis-specific EU residency, we recommend the hybrid: 90d hot EU + 365d cold encrypted archive (retrieval 48–72h).
- PII redaction: we can run a preservation pass and produce redacted search indices for the EU scope to reduce exposure during retrievals. That will be part of the evidence snapshot process.
- Evidence delivery cadence: 
  * Phase 1 (within 7 business days of decision): configuration export, access logs for last 30 days, service-config manifests.
  * Phase 2 (within 14 business days): index snapshots and redacted search export covering the requested retention windows.
  * Phase 3 (ongoing): automated monthly snapshot delivery to the escrow location you specify.

We'll need an explicit amendment to include the retrieval SLA and encryption-at-rest location. Mina, please have Legal confirm any wording for the EU carveout.
